sanskrit: arasaṃ prācyaṃ viṣam arasaṃ yad udīcyam | athedam adharācyaṃ karambheṇa vi kalpate ||
english: Powerless is the poison from the east, powerless what comes from the north; and this here from below is dissolved by the grain-gruel karamba.

sanskrit: karambhaṃ kṛtvā tiryaṃ pīvasphākam udārathim | kṣudhā kila tvā duṣṭano jakṣivāṃsaṃ na rūrupaḥ ||
english: Having placed the karamba grain-gruel crosswise — full-fatted and excellently conveyed — hunger, they say, has devoured you, O malicious one; let it not wound.

sanskrit: vi te madaṃ madavati śarum iva pātayāmasi | pra tvā carum iva yeṣantaṃ vacasā sthāpayāmasi ||
english: Your intoxication, O intoxicating one, we cause to fall like an arrow shot; you who surge forward like a boiling cauldron, we bring to a standstill by our utterance.

sanskrit: pari grāmam ivācitaṃ pari tvā sthāpayāmasi | tiṣṭhā vṛkṣa iva sthāmann abhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||
english: As one heaps up around a village, so we heap up around you; stand firm as a tree in its standing-place — in the pit dug by the spade let it not wound.

sanskrit: pavastais tvā pary akrīṇan dūrśebhir ajinair uta | prakrīr asi tvam oṣadhe 'bhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||
english: They have bought you round about with pavasta-grain and with hides of distant aspect; you are a herb of wide purchase — in the pit dug by the spade let it not wound.

sanskrit: āvidya dyāvāpṛthivī āvidya bhagam aśvinā | āvidya brahmaṇaspatiṃ kṛṇomy arasaṃ viṣam ||
english: Invoking Heaven-and-Earth, invoking Bhaga and the two Aśvins, invoking Bṛhaspati, I render the poison powerless.

sanskrit: arasaṃ hed idaṃ viṣaṃ yathainad aham āśiṣam | utainad adyāt puruṣo bhavād id agadaḥ punaḥ ||
english: Verily powerless shall this poison be, even as I have wished it to be; moreover, let a person eat of it — he shall be free from disease again.

sanskrit: mā bibher na mariṣyasi pari tvā pāmi viśvataḥ | rasaṃ viṣasya nāvidam udnaḥ phenam adann iva ||
english: Fear not — you shall not die; I protect you on every side. I have not known the potency of the poison, as one eating the foam of water.

sanskrit: apāvocad apavaktā prathamo daivyo bhiṣak | samakṣam indra gā iva yā vāco viṣadūṣaṇīḥ ||
english: The avertive speaker, the first divine physician, has spoken away — even before Indra's eyes, like cows — those words that are the bane of poison.

sanskrit: yac ca piṣṭaṃ yac cāpiṣṭaṃ yad digdhaṃ yac ca dehyam | devāḥ sarvasya vidvāṃso 'rasaṃ kṛṇutā viṣam ||
english: Whatever has been ground, whatever unground, whatever has been smeared, whatever may be smeared — O Gods, knowing all things, render the poison powerless.

sanskrit: kṣetriyāt tvā nirṛtyā jāmiśaṃsād druho muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśāt | anāgasaṃ brahmaṇā tvā kṛṇomi śive te dyāvāpṛthivī abhūtām ||
english: From hereditary disease, from Nirṛti, from the calumny of kinsmen, from treachery, from the noose of Varuṇa I release you. Sinless I make you by sacred utterance; may Heaven-and-Earth be propitious to you.

sanskrit: śaṃ te agniḥ sahādbhir astu śaṃ gāvaḥ sahauṣadhībhiḥ | śam antarikṣaṃ sahavātam astu te śaṃ te bhavantu pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
english: Auspicious to you be Agni together with the waters; auspicious the cows together with the herbs; auspicious to you be the atmosphere together with the wind; auspicious to you be the four cardinal directions.

sanskrit: yā devīḥ pradiśaś catasro vātapatnīr abhi sūryo vicaṣṭe | tāsv etaṃ jarasa ā dadhāmi pra yakṣma etu nirṛtiḥ parācaiḥ ||
english: The four divine cardinal directions, whose consort is the Wind, upon which the Sun looks forth — in them I place this one unto old age; let the yakṣma-disease go forth, let Nirṛti depart into the beyond.

sanskrit: sūryam ṛtaṃ tamaso grāhyā yathā devā muñcanto asṛjan nir enasaḥ | evā tvā kṣetriyān nirṛtyā jāmiśaṃsād druho muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśāt ||
english: Just as the Gods, releasing the Sun, the embodiment of cosmic order, from the grip of darkness, sent it forth free of sin — so from hereditary disease, from Nirṛti, from the calumny of kinsmen, from treachery, from the noose of Varuṇa I release you.

sanskrit: amoci yakṣmād duritād avadyād druhaḥ pāśād grāhyāś cod amoci | jahad avartim avidat syonām apy abhūd bhadre sukṛtasya loke ||
english: Released is he from yakṣma-disease, from misfortune, from disgrace, from the noose of treachery — and also released from the grip of demonic seizure. Casting off ill fortune he has found ease; he has entered the blessed world of those who have done good.
